numbers.v: 9: eight printed parts and one lens
any 35 mm film in its standard shell
one plastic lens, 32 mm focal length, 12 mm across
small f/16, middle f/11, large f/9.5
one speed, about a three-hundredth of a second; held open for time pictures
from 1.3 m with the small dot; stand 2 m (two big steps) or more
8 holes of the film = 38 mm = one picture

intro.title: CURVE 35
intro.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.715
CURVE 35.

2
00:00:01.715 --> 00:00:03.167
Build your own film camera.

3
00:00:03.717 --> 00:00:08.096
The camera is 9 pieces you put together: 8 printed parts and one lens.

4
00:00:08.646 --> 00:00:11.843
It goes together with no tools, no glue and no screws.

5
00:00:12.393 --> 00:00:15.337
You can print it free, from the files, or buy the kit.

6
00:00:15.887 --> 00:00:21.130
CURVE 35 is for ages 14 and up; younger builders can build it with an adult.

7
00:00:21.680 --> 00:00:26.155
This film walks through every step: 10 to build it, 6 to load the film,

8
00:00:26.155 --> 00:00:30.974
4 for every picture, 2 to take the film out, and 3 for the pinhole experiment.

b1.title: Spool in
b1.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.470
Ten steps.

2
00:00:01.470 --> 00:00:03.915
Steps 1 to 4 make the dark box.

3
00:00:03.915 --> 00:00:07.785
Steps 5 to 10 put the orange front plate on it, with the shutter,

4
00:00:07.785 --> 00:00:09.071
the wheel and the lens.

5
00:00:09.621 --> 00:00:10.681
Build step one.

6
00:00:10.681 --> 00:00:13.381
Take the spool, the part with the big red knob.

7
00:00:13.381 --> 00:00:17.616
Slide it, knob up, into the round chamber on the right, seen from behind.

8
00:00:17.616 --> 00:00:20.226
Its plain end goes into the slot in the floor,

9
00:00:20.226 --> 00:00:23.461
and the knob's neck into the slot in the roof.

10
00:00:23.461 --> 00:00:26.741
Check it: the big red knob sits on top of the camera and turns.

11
00:00:26.741 --> 00:00:29.946
The spool, its shaft and its knob are one piece,

12
00:00:29.946 --> 00:00:32.213
because this is the part you turn hardest.

b2.title: Wind knob in
b2.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.435
Step two.

2
00:00:01.435 --> 00:00:04.560
Slide the small green knob into the slot on the left.

3
00:00:04.560 --> 00:00:05.745
Give it a turn.

4
00:00:05.745 --> 00:00:08.500
It turns, and it only comes out backwards.

5
00:00:08.500 --> 00:00:11.040
This knob will turn the film's own spool:

6
00:00:11.040 --> 00:00:14.010
its forked end fits over a bar inside the film.

7
00:00:14.010 --> 00:00:17.765
So the green knob winds each picture back into the film's shell,

8
00:00:17.765 --> 00:00:20.077
and the red knob is where the film starts.

b3.title: Frame wheel into the back
b3.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.405
Step three.

2
00:00:01.405 --> 00:00:03.405
Lay the back down, inside up.

3
00:00:03.405 --> 00:00:06.790
Hold the blue frame wheel with its dial just past the edge.

4
00:00:06.790 --> 00:00:11.312
Lay its neck in the fork, then slide it toward the long round post until its teeth

5
00:00:11.312 --> 00:00:12.850
touch the end of the post.

6
00:00:12.850 --> 00:00:15.930
The wheel turns freely, and it does not lift out.

7
00:00:15.930 --> 00:00:20.030
If it does lift out, it was not slid home: slide it toward the edge,

8
00:00:20.030 --> 00:00:22.494
press it down into the fork, and slide it back.

b4.title: Close the dark box
b4.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.375
Step four.

2
00:00:01.375 --> 00:00:03.935
Press the back on until both ends click.

3
00:00:03.935 --> 00:00:05.000
Two clicks.

4
00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:07.100
Now try to pull it off: it stays.

5
00:00:07.100 --> 00:00:09.515
Pinch the two pads and it lets go.

6
00:00:09.515 --> 00:00:13.615
A nub on a springy finger at each end comes up behind a bar on the body,

7
00:00:13.615 --> 00:00:17.255
and a ridge all round the back sits in a groove to keep the light out.

8
00:00:17.255 --> 00:00:18.695
This is the dark box.

9
00:00:18.695 --> 00:00:20.876
Everything else goes on its front.

b5.title: Shutter onto its peg
b5.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:02.445
Step five, and the front plate.

2
00:00:02.445 --> 00:00:04.000
Lay it face down.

3
00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:07.973
Drop the shutter onto the round peg near the top edge, with the rocker,

4
00:00:07.973 --> 00:00:10.535
the bar across its top, hanging over the edge.

5
00:00:10.535 --> 00:00:14.780
The rocker sits just outside the edge; the shutter swings and clicks.

6
00:00:14.780 --> 00:00:17.695
If it will not lie flat, it is upside down.

7
00:00:17.695 --> 00:00:21.643
The peg is the shutter's pivot, and the shutter's own rim is its spring.

b6.title: Aperture wheel onto its peg
b6.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.525
Step six.

2
00:00:01.525 --> 00:00:03.585
Pick the plate up and hold it flat.

3
00:00:03.585 --> 00:00:08.155
Drop the aperture wheel onto the other peg, handle down through the curved slot.

4
00:00:08.155 --> 00:00:12.165
The handle sticks out of the front, and the wheel clicks into three places.

5
00:00:12.165 --> 00:00:16.260
If the wheel will not lie flat, its handle is not in the slot yet.

6
00:00:16.260 --> 00:00:20.982
The wheel carries three holes of different sizes, and its rim is a spring too.

b7.title: Camera onto the plate
b7.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.470
Step seven.

2
00:00:01.470 --> 00:00:02.735
Keep the plate flat.

3
00:00:02.735 --> 00:00:06.985
Lower the camera onto it, front down, a little high and a little to one side,

4
00:00:06.985 --> 00:00:09.915
until its four pockets drop over the plate's four feet.

5
00:00:09.915 --> 00:00:13.080
The camera lies flat on the plate and nothing rocks.

6
00:00:13.080 --> 00:00:17.985
If it rocks, move it about a few millimetres: the feet drop in at one place only.

7
00:00:17.985 --> 00:00:22.675
Each pocket is open at one corner: that is the way in, and the only way out.

b8.title: Slide the plate across
b8.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.390
Step eight.

2
00:00:01.390 --> 00:00:04.140
Pinch camera and plate together and turn them over.

3
00:00:04.140 --> 00:00:07.035
Slide the plate sideways until it stops.

4
00:00:07.035 --> 00:00:11.975
The point on the plate's top edge now lines up with the middle line on top of the

5
00:00:11.975 --> 00:00:12.094
camera.

6
00:00:12.094 --> 00:00:16.345
If it will not slide, it is not flat on the camera, so go back one step.

7
00:00:16.345 --> 00:00:19.540
Now the lips on the feet are under the camera's skin,

8
00:00:19.540 --> 00:00:21.760
and the plate can no longer be lifted off.

b9.title: Slide the plate down
b9.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.450
Step nine.

2
00:00:01.450 --> 00:00:03.730
Slide the plate down until it clicks.

3
00:00:03.730 --> 00:00:07.295
One click, and its top edge is level with the top of the camera.

4
00:00:07.295 --> 00:00:08.325
No click?

5
00:00:08.325 --> 00:00:11.210
Press the plate flat against the body while you slide.

6
00:00:11.210 --> 00:00:14.770
The hooks are home and a springy tongue has dropped behind a bump.

7
00:00:14.770 --> 00:00:19.225
To come off, the plate has to go up past the click, then sideways, then away.

8
00:00:19.225 --> 00:00:20.944
A knock cannot do all three.

b10.title: Lens in
b10.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:02.185
Step ten, the last one.

2
00:00:02.185 --> 00:00:06.475
Press the lens into the round pocket on the front, bulge outward, until it stops.

3
00:00:06.475 --> 00:00:09.855
It sits level and stays in when you shake the camera.

4
00:00:09.855 --> 00:00:12.565
Three small ribs in the pocket squeeze the lens;

5
00:00:12.565 --> 00:00:15.075
nothing else in the camera is held by a squeeze.

6
00:00:15.075 --> 00:00:18.805
If the lens is loose, or will not go in, tell whoever made the kit.

7
00:00:18.805 --> 00:00:20.580
Press the rocker: click.

8
00:00:20.580 --> 00:00:22.695
Slide the handle: three clicks.

9
00:00:22.695 --> 00:00:23.337
Done.

f1.title: Open the back
f1.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.650
Loading the film.

2
00:00:01.650 --> 00:00:04.865
Find some shade first: never do this in bright sun.

3
00:00:04.865 --> 00:00:08.475
Pinch the two pads, top and bottom, and lift the back off.

4
00:00:08.475 --> 00:00:13.675
The blue frame wheel comes away with the back, so lay the back down somewhere safe,

5
00:00:13.675 --> 00:00:14.010
inside up.

6
00:00:14.010 --> 00:00:17.695
From here until the back is closed again, keep the film out of the sun.

7
00:00:17.695 --> 00:00:20.347
Next, the green knob goes into the film.

f2.title: Knob into the film
f2.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:03.015
Slide the small green knob out of the camera.

2
00:00:03.015 --> 00:00:05.960
Push its forked end into the hollow end of the film.

3
00:00:05.960 --> 00:00:09.745
Now turn the knob: the spool inside the film turns with it.

4
00:00:09.745 --> 00:00:10.865
Wrong end?

5
00:00:10.865 --> 00:00:13.685
The other end of the film has a peg sticking out.

6
00:00:13.685 --> 00:00:16.720
The fork straddles a bar inside the film's spool,

7
00:00:16.720 --> 00:00:19.728
so from now on this knob turns the film's own spool.

f3.title: Film into its chamber
f3.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:03.625
Slide the film and the knob in together, on the left,

2
00:00:03.625 --> 00:00:06.455
with the film's lip pointing to the middle of the camera.

3
00:00:06.455 --> 00:00:08.535
Keep them together as they go in.

4
00:00:08.535 --> 00:00:13.435
The film sits flat in its chamber, and the green knob sits in its slot on top,

5
00:00:13.435 --> 00:00:15.105
just as it did before.

6
00:00:15.105 --> 00:00:17.170
If the film will not sit flat,

7
00:00:17.170 --> 00:00:20.042
lift it out and try again with the lip facing the middle.

f4.title: Catch the film's tip
f4.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:04.070
Turn the big red knob until the slot in its spool faces you.

2
00:00:04.070 --> 00:00:07.050
Pull the film across and tuck its tip into the slot.

3
00:00:07.050 --> 00:00:09.160
Give the big red knob one turn.

4
00:00:09.160 --> 00:00:12.730
The film is caught, and it lies over the two curved rails.

5
00:00:12.730 --> 00:00:15.980
If the tip slips out, tuck it deeper and turn again.

6
00:00:15.980 --> 00:00:18.595
The film lies on a curve around the lens:

7
00:00:18.595 --> 00:00:22.399
that curve is why one simple lens can be sharp from corner to corner.

f5.title: Close the back
f5.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.570
Close the back.

2
00:00:01.570 --> 00:00:04.500
Press until you hear two clicks, one at each end.

3
00:00:04.500 --> 00:00:06.910
Keep it shut until the film is out again.

4
00:00:06.910 --> 00:00:10.325
The frame wheel's teeth press on the film's top edge.

5
00:00:10.325 --> 00:00:13.300
If they are not in the film's holes yet, do not worry:

6
00:00:13.300 --> 00:00:15.585
the first turn of the knob drops them in.

7
00:00:15.585 --> 00:00:17.895
From now on, the film is in the dark.

f6.title: Wind the film out
f6.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:03.920
Turn the big red knob the way the picture shows until it stops:

2
00:00:03.920 --> 00:00:07.465
about 25 turns for a film of 24 pictures, about 33 for 36.

3
00:00:07.465 --> 00:00:12.775
While you turn, the arrow on the blue dial goes round and round: the film is moving.

4
00:00:12.775 --> 00:00:18.495
If the arrow does not move, open the back in the shade and tuck the film in again.

5
00:00:18.495 --> 00:00:19.905
When the knob stops, stop.

6
00:00:19.905 --> 00:00:23.460
Every picture you take will be wound back into the shell,

7
00:00:23.460 --> 00:00:24.788
where light cannot reach it.

p1.title: Pick a dot
p1.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:04.502
Four steps for every picture: choose a dot, aim, press, wind.

2
00:00:05.052 --> 00:00:06.842
Taking a picture, step one.

3
00:00:06.842 --> 00:00:09.352
Slide the handle on the front to a dot.

4
00:00:09.352 --> 00:00:12.337
The chart shows which one, for your film and the light.

5
00:00:12.337 --> 00:00:13.947
It clicks at each dot.

6
00:00:13.947 --> 00:00:16.677
The dot shows the size of the hole behind it,

7
00:00:16.677 --> 00:00:20.197
and each dot lets in about twice the light of the one before.

8
00:00:20.197 --> 00:00:25.124
When even the largest dot is too small for a snap, take a time picture instead.

9
00:00:25.674 --> 00:00:27.359
Lesson 4, Aperture.

10
00:00:27.359 --> 00:00:30.124
The size of the hole sets how much light gets in;

11
00:00:30.124 --> 00:00:32.615
each f-number step halves or doubles it.

p2.title: Aim
p2.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.335
Step two: aim.

2
00:00:01.335 --> 00:00:03.870
Look along the middle line on top,

3
00:00:03.870 --> 00:00:06.795
from the edge of the pad at the back to the point at the front.

4
00:00:06.795 --> 00:00:09.580
The picture fits between the two outer lines.

5
00:00:09.580 --> 00:00:13.265
Stand at least two big steps away from what you are photographing.

6
00:00:13.265 --> 00:00:17.500
Nearer than that and the picture is not sharp, because the focus is fixed.

7
00:00:17.500 --> 00:00:20.471
Put what matters in the middle: it is sharpest there.

p3.title: Press the rocker
p3.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.365
Step three.

2
00:00:01.365 --> 00:00:02.325
Hold still.

3
00:00:02.325 --> 00:00:05.835
Press the raised side of the rocker flat, in one quick press.

4
00:00:05.835 --> 00:00:06.850
One click.

5
00:00:06.850 --> 00:00:10.595
Now the other side is up: that is the side to press next time.

6
00:00:10.595 --> 00:00:14.780
If the rocker stops level, the shutter is open, so press it on down.

7
00:00:14.780 --> 00:00:17.895
A window in the shutter passes the hole as it swings:

8
00:00:17.895 --> 00:00:21.540
a quick press lets light in for about a three-hundredth of a second.

9
00:00:22.090 --> 00:00:23.820
Lesson 5, The shutter.

10
00:00:23.820 --> 00:00:26.525
A shutter lets light in for a set instant;

11
00:00:26.525 --> 00:00:29.712
this one is a plastic blade whose own rim is its spring.

p4.title: Wind on
p4.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:02.245
Step four: wind on.

2
00:00:02.245 --> 00:00:06.721
Turn the small green knob the way the picture shows until the arrow on the blue dial

3
00:00:06.721 --> 00:00:07.930
has gone once round.

4
00:00:07.930 --> 00:00:10.395
Keep your other hand off the big red knob.

5
00:00:10.395 --> 00:00:13.080
The arrow points at its mark on the body again.

6
00:00:13.080 --> 00:00:18.100
If the knob is stiff, stop and take your hand off the red knob: never force it.

7
00:00:18.100 --> 00:00:21.146
One turn of the dial is one picture's length of film.

8
00:00:21.696 --> 00:00:23.686
Lesson 6, Winding on.

9
00:00:23.686 --> 00:00:26.321
The film's own holes turn the frame wheel,

10
00:00:26.321 --> 00:00:29.147
so one turn of the dial is exactly one picture.

o1.title: Wind it all back
o1.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.420
Two steps.

2
00:00:01.420 --> 00:00:03.763
Then the film goes to a lab to be developed.

3
00:00:04.313 --> 00:00:05.648
The film is finished.

4
00:00:05.648 --> 00:00:11.288
After the last picture, keep turning the small green knob until the arrow on the

5
00:00:11.288 --> 00:00:12.053
dial stops moving.

6
00:00:12.053 --> 00:00:13.303
Then give it three more turns.

7
00:00:13.303 --> 00:00:17.688
The arrow no longer moves: all the film is back in its shell, in the dark.

8
00:00:17.688 --> 00:00:20.308
Only now is it safe to open the back.

9
00:00:20.308 --> 00:00:25.390
If the arrow is still moving, keep winding; never open the back before it stops.

o2.title: Take the film out
o2.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.525
Open the back.

2
00:00:01.525 --> 00:00:04.665
Slide the film out with its knob and pull the knob off.

3
00:00:04.665 --> 00:00:08.350
The film's tip is inside the shell, or just peeping out.

4
00:00:08.350 --> 00:00:12.665
Send the film off with your developing card, or take it to any photo lab:

5
00:00:12.665 --> 00:00:16.280
any lab that develops 35 millimetre film can do it.

6
00:00:16.280 --> 00:00:18.990
Ask for scans, and keep the negatives.

7
00:00:18.990 --> 00:00:20.364
They are the originals.

h1.title: Get or make the disc
h1.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.965
The pinhole experiment.

2
00:00:01.965 --> 00:00:04.960
Take the pinhole disc from the bag, or make one.

3
00:00:04.960 --> 00:00:09.776
To make one, ask an adult to cut a square about 10 mm across from a clean drinks can

4
00:00:09.776 --> 00:00:12.900
with kitchen scissors, and to snip off its corners.

5
00:00:12.900 --> 00:00:15.470
Lay it on card, press a pin into the middle,

6
00:00:15.470 --> 00:00:17.900
then push just until the tip comes through.

7
00:00:17.900 --> 00:00:21.922
Hold it up to a lamp: you should see one tiny round point of light.

8
00:00:22.472 --> 00:00:24.237
Lesson 1, The pinhole.

9
00:00:24.237 --> 00:00:26.372
Light travels in straight lines,

10
00:00:26.372 --> 00:00:31.212
so a small hole lets through from each point of a scene only the rays lined up with

11
00:00:31.212 --> 00:00:32.734
it: an upside-down picture.

h2.title: Disc and ring in
h2.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.730
Leave the lens out.

2
00:00:01.730 --> 00:00:05.242
Lay the disc flat in the round pocket, hole in the middle,

3
00:00:05.242 --> 00:00:08.120
and press the pinhole ring in on top of it until it stops.

4
00:00:08.120 --> 00:00:11.565
The disc covers the hole in the floor of the pocket all round.

5
00:00:11.565 --> 00:00:14.625
The ring stands a little proud and does not wobble.

6
00:00:14.625 --> 00:00:19.255
Same plate, same pocket: with the disc and ring it is a pinhole camera.

7
00:00:19.255 --> 00:00:22.142
To change back, lift the ring out with a fingernail.

h3.title: Take a pinhole picture
h3.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.880
Set the large dot.

2
00:00:01.880 --> 00:00:03.980
Stand the camera on something steady.

3
00:00:03.980 --> 00:00:09.900
Hold the rocker level to open it, count, then press it down, and wind on.

4
00:00:09.900 --> 00:00:11.705
With ISO 400 film: in sun, open and shut.

5
00:00:11.705 --> 00:00:13.250
Cloud, count 1.

6
00:00:13.250 --> 00:00:14.800
Shade, count 3.

7
00:00:14.800 --> 00:00:17.130
Indoors by a window, count 40.

8
00:00:17.130 --> 00:00:21.150
The pinhole lets in about 150 times less light than the large dot,

9
00:00:21.150 --> 00:00:23.773
so a pinhole picture is counted, not snapped.

outro.title: Next: the lessons and the final roll
outro.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:02.070
That is the whole camera.

2
00:00:02.070 --> 00:00:08.702
The 9 lessons explain how it works, one idea each, at curve35.com/lessons.

3
00:00:09.252 --> 00:00:15.122
The final roll: 24 frames that use every lesson, and a rubric to grade it.

4
00:00:15.122 --> 00:00:17.846
It is at curve35.com/final.

5
00:00:18.396 --> 00:00:23.385
If a step will not go, the help page is at curve35.com/help.

video.vtt:
WEBVTT

1
00:00:00.600 --> 00:00:01.715
CURVE 35.

2
00:00:01.715 --> 00:00:03.167
Build your own film camera.

3
00:00:03.717 --> 00:00:08.096
The camera is 9 pieces you put together: 8 printed parts and one lens.

4
00:00:08.646 --> 00:00:11.843
It goes together with no tools, no glue and no screws.

5
00:00:12.393 --> 00:00:15.337
You can print it free, from the files, or buy the kit.

6
00:00:15.887 --> 00:00:21.130
CURVE 35 is for ages 14 and up; younger builders can build it with an adult.

7
00:00:21.680 --> 00:00:26.155
This film walks through every step: 10 to build it, 6 to load the film,

8
00:00:26.155 --> 00:00:30.974
4 for every picture, 2 to take the film out, and 3 for the pinhole experiment.

9
00:00:32.700 --> 00:00:33.570
Ten steps.

10
00:00:33.570 --> 00:00:36.015
Steps 1 to 4 make the dark box.

11
00:00:36.015 --> 00:00:39.885
Steps 5 to 10 put the orange front plate on it, with the shutter,

12
00:00:39.885 --> 00:00:41.171
the wheel and the lens.

13
00:00:41.721 --> 00:00:42.781
Build step one.

14
00:00:42.781 --> 00:00:45.481
Take the spool, the part with the big red knob.

15
00:00:45.481 --> 00:00:49.716
Slide it, knob up, into the round chamber on the right, seen from behind.

16
00:00:49.716 --> 00:00:52.326
Its plain end goes into the slot in the floor,

17
00:00:52.326 --> 00:00:55.561
and the knob's neck into the slot in the roof.

18
00:00:55.561 --> 00:00:58.841
Check it: the big red knob sits on top of the camera and turns.

19
00:00:58.841 --> 00:01:02.046
The spool, its shaft and its knob are one piece,

20
00:01:02.046 --> 00:01:04.313
because this is the part you turn hardest.

21
00:01:06.033 --> 00:01:06.868
Step two.

22
00:01:06.868 --> 00:01:09.993
Slide the small green knob into the slot on the left.

23
00:01:09.993 --> 00:01:11.178
Give it a turn.

24
00:01:11.178 --> 00:01:13.933
It turns, and it only comes out backwards.

25
00:01:13.933 --> 00:01:16.473
This knob will turn the film's own spool:

26
00:01:16.473 --> 00:01:19.443
its forked end fits over a bar inside the film.

27
00:01:19.443 --> 00:01:23.198
So the green knob winds each picture back into the film's shell,

28
00:01:23.198 --> 00:01:25.510
and the red knob is where the film starts.

29
00:01:27.233 --> 00:01:28.038
Step three.

30
00:01:28.038 --> 00:01:30.038
Lay the back down, inside up.

31
00:01:30.038 --> 00:01:33.423
Hold the blue frame wheel with its dial just past the edge.

32
00:01:33.423 --> 00:01:37.945
Lay its neck in the fork, then slide it toward the long round post until its teeth

33
00:01:37.945 --> 00:01:39.483
touch the end of the post.

34
00:01:39.483 --> 00:01:42.563
The wheel turns freely, and it does not lift out.

35
00:01:42.563 --> 00:01:46.663
If it does lift out, it was not slid home: slide it toward the edge,

36
00:01:46.663 --> 00:01:49.127
press it down into the fork, and slide it back.

37
00:01:50.833 --> 00:01:51.608
Step four.

38
00:01:51.608 --> 00:01:54.168
Press the back on until both ends click.

39
00:01:54.168 --> 00:01:55.233
Two clicks.

40
00:01:55.233 --> 00:01:57.333
Now try to pull it off: it stays.

41
00:01:57.333 --> 00:01:59.748
Pinch the two pads and it lets go.

42
00:01:59.748 --> 00:02:03.848
A nub on a springy finger at each end comes up behind a bar on the body,

43
00:02:03.848 --> 00:02:07.488
and a ridge all round the back sits in a groove to keep the light out.

44
00:02:07.488 --> 00:02:08.928
This is the dark box.

45
00:02:08.928 --> 00:02:11.109
Everything else goes on its front.

46
00:02:12.833 --> 00:02:14.678
Step five, and the front plate.

47
00:02:14.678 --> 00:02:16.233
Lay it face down.

48
00:02:16.233 --> 00:02:20.206
Drop the shutter onto the round peg near the top edge, with the rocker,

49
00:02:20.206 --> 00:02:22.768
the bar across its top, hanging over the edge.

50
00:02:22.768 --> 00:02:27.013
The rocker sits just outside the edge; the shutter swings and clicks.

51
00:02:27.013 --> 00:02:29.928
If it will not lie flat, it is upside down.

52
00:02:29.928 --> 00:02:33.876
The peg is the shutter's pivot, and the shutter's own rim is its spring.

53
00:02:35.600 --> 00:02:36.525
Step six.

54
00:02:36.525 --> 00:02:38.585
Pick the plate up and hold it flat.

55
00:02:38.585 --> 00:02:43.155
Drop the aperture wheel onto the other peg, handle down through the curved slot.

56
00:02:43.155 --> 00:02:47.165
The handle sticks out of the front, and the wheel clicks into three places.

57
00:02:47.165 --> 00:02:51.260
If the wheel will not lie flat, its handle is not in the slot yet.

58
00:02:51.260 --> 00:02:55.982
The wheel carries three holes of different sizes, and its rim is a spring too.

59
00:02:57.700 --> 00:02:58.570
Step seven.

60
00:02:58.570 --> 00:02:59.835
Keep the plate flat.

61
00:02:59.835 --> 00:03:04.085
Lower the camera onto it, front down, a little high and a little to one side,

62
00:03:04.085 --> 00:03:07.015
until its four pockets drop over the plate's four feet.

63
00:03:07.015 --> 00:03:10.180
The camera lies flat on the plate and nothing rocks.

64
00:03:10.180 --> 00:03:15.085
If it rocks, move it about a few millimetres: the feet drop in at one place only.

65
00:03:15.085 --> 00:03:19.775
Each pocket is open at one corner: that is the way in, and the only way out.

66
00:03:21.500 --> 00:03:22.290
Step eight.

67
00:03:22.290 --> 00:03:25.040
Pinch camera and plate together and turn them over.

68
00:03:25.040 --> 00:03:27.935
Slide the plate sideways until it stops.

69
00:03:27.935 --> 00:03:32.875
The point on the plate's top edge now lines up with the middle line on top of the

70
00:03:32.875 --> 00:03:32.994
camera.

71
00:03:32.994 --> 00:03:37.245
If it will not slide, it is not flat on the camera, so go back one step.

72
00:03:37.245 --> 00:03:40.440
Now the lips on the feet are under the camera's skin,

73
00:03:40.440 --> 00:03:42.660
and the plate can no longer be lifted off.

74
00:03:44.367 --> 00:03:45.217
Step nine.

75
00:03:45.217 --> 00:03:47.497
Slide the plate down until it clicks.

76
00:03:47.497 --> 00:03:51.062
One click, and its top edge is level with the top of the camera.

77
00:03:51.062 --> 00:03:52.092
No click?

78
00:03:52.092 --> 00:03:54.977
Press the plate flat against the body while you slide.

79
00:03:54.977 --> 00:03:58.537
The hooks are home and a springy tongue has dropped behind a bump.

80
00:03:58.537 --> 00:04:02.992
To come off, the plate has to go up past the click, then sideways, then away.

81
00:04:02.992 --> 00:04:04.711
A knock cannot do all three.

82
00:04:06.433 --> 00:04:08.018
Step ten, the last one.

83
00:04:08.018 --> 00:04:12.308
Press the lens into the round pocket on the front, bulge outward, until it stops.

84
00:04:12.308 --> 00:04:15.688
It sits level and stays in when you shake the camera.

85
00:04:15.688 --> 00:04:18.398
Three small ribs in the pocket squeeze the lens;

86
00:04:18.398 --> 00:04:20.908
nothing else in the camera is held by a squeeze.

87
00:04:20.908 --> 00:04:24.638
If the lens is loose, or will not go in, tell whoever made the kit.

88
00:04:24.638 --> 00:04:26.413
Press the rocker: click.

89
00:04:26.413 --> 00:04:28.528
Slide the handle: three clicks.

90
00:04:28.528 --> 00:04:29.170
Done.

91
00:04:30.900 --> 00:04:31.950
Loading the film.

92
00:04:31.950 --> 00:04:35.165
Find some shade first: never do this in bright sun.

93
00:04:35.165 --> 00:04:38.775
Pinch the two pads, top and bottom, and lift the back off.

94
00:04:38.775 --> 00:04:43.975
The blue frame wheel comes away with the back, so lay the back down somewhere safe,

95
00:04:43.975 --> 00:04:44.310
inside up.

96
00:04:44.310 --> 00:04:47.995
From here until the back is closed again, keep the film out of the sun.

97
00:04:47.995 --> 00:04:50.647
Next, the green knob goes into the film.

98
00:04:52.367 --> 00:04:54.782
Slide the small green knob out of the camera.

99
00:04:54.782 --> 00:04:57.727
Push its forked end into the hollow end of the film.

100
00:04:57.727 --> 00:05:01.512
Now turn the knob: the spool inside the film turns with it.

101
00:05:01.512 --> 00:05:02.632
Wrong end?

102
00:05:02.632 --> 00:05:05.452
The other end of the film has a peg sticking out.

103
00:05:05.452 --> 00:05:08.487
The fork straddles a bar inside the film's spool,

104
00:05:08.487 --> 00:05:11.495
so from now on this knob turns the film's own spool.

105
00:05:13.200 --> 00:05:16.225
Slide the film and the knob in together, on the left,

106
00:05:16.225 --> 00:05:19.055
with the film's lip pointing to the middle of the camera.

107
00:05:19.055 --> 00:05:21.135
Keep them together as they go in.

108
00:05:21.135 --> 00:05:26.035
The film sits flat in its chamber, and the green knob sits in its slot on top,

109
00:05:26.035 --> 00:05:27.705
just as it did before.

110
00:05:27.705 --> 00:05:29.770
If the film will not sit flat,

111
00:05:29.770 --> 00:05:32.642
lift it out and try again with the lip facing the middle.

112
00:05:34.367 --> 00:05:37.837
Turn the big red knob until the slot in its spool faces you.

113
00:05:37.837 --> 00:05:40.817
Pull the film across and tuck its tip into the slot.

114
00:05:40.817 --> 00:05:42.927
Give the big red knob one turn.

115
00:05:42.927 --> 00:05:46.497
The film is caught, and it lies over the two curved rails.

116
00:05:46.497 --> 00:05:49.747
If the tip slips out, tuck it deeper and turn again.

117
00:05:49.747 --> 00:05:52.362
The film lies on a curve around the lens:

118
00:05:52.362 --> 00:05:56.166
that curve is why one simple lens can be sharp from corner to corner.

119
00:05:57.867 --> 00:05:58.837
Close the back.

120
00:05:58.837 --> 00:06:01.767
Press until you hear two clicks, one at each end.

121
00:06:01.767 --> 00:06:04.177
Keep it shut until the film is out again.

122
00:06:04.177 --> 00:06:07.592
The frame wheel's teeth press on the film's top edge.

123
00:06:07.592 --> 00:06:10.567
If they are not in the film's holes yet, do not worry:

124
00:06:10.567 --> 00:06:12.852
the first turn of the knob drops them in.

125
00:06:12.852 --> 00:06:15.162
From now on, the film is in the dark.

126
00:06:16.867 --> 00:06:20.187
Turn the big red knob the way the picture shows until it stops:

127
00:06:20.187 --> 00:06:23.732
about 25 turns for a film of 24 pictures, about 33 for 36.

128
00:06:23.732 --> 00:06:29.042
While you turn, the arrow on the blue dial goes round and round: the film is moving.

129
00:06:29.042 --> 00:06:34.762
If the arrow does not move, open the back in the shade and tuck the film in again.

130
00:06:34.762 --> 00:06:36.172
When the knob stops, stop.

131
00:06:36.172 --> 00:06:39.727
Every picture you take will be wound back into the shell,

132
00:06:39.727 --> 00:06:41.055
where light cannot reach it.

133
00:06:42.767 --> 00:06:46.669
Four steps for every picture: choose a dot, aim, press, wind.

134
00:06:47.219 --> 00:06:49.009
Taking a picture, step one.

135
00:06:49.009 --> 00:06:51.519
Slide the handle on the front to a dot.

136
00:06:51.519 --> 00:06:54.504
The chart shows which one, for your film and the light.

137
00:06:54.504 --> 00:06:56.114
It clicks at each dot.

138
00:06:56.114 --> 00:06:58.844
The dot shows the size of the hole behind it,

139
00:06:58.844 --> 00:07:02.364
and each dot lets in about twice the light of the one before.

140
00:07:02.364 --> 00:07:07.291
When even the largest dot is too small for a snap, take a time picture instead.

141
00:07:07.841 --> 00:07:09.526
Lesson 4, Aperture.

142
00:07:09.526 --> 00:07:12.291
The size of the hole sets how much light gets in;

143
00:07:12.291 --> 00:07:14.782
each f-number step halves or doubles it.

144
00:07:16.500 --> 00:07:17.235
Step two: aim.

145
00:07:17.235 --> 00:07:19.770
Look along the middle line on top,

146
00:07:19.770 --> 00:07:22.695
from the edge of the pad at the back to the point at the front.

147
00:07:22.695 --> 00:07:25.480
The picture fits between the two outer lines.

148
00:07:25.480 --> 00:07:29.165
Stand at least two big steps away from what you are photographing.

149
00:07:29.165 --> 00:07:33.400
Nearer than that and the picture is not sharp, because the focus is fixed.

150
00:07:33.400 --> 00:07:36.371
Put what matters in the middle: it is sharpest there.

151
00:07:38.100 --> 00:07:38.865
Step three.

152
00:07:38.865 --> 00:07:39.825
Hold still.

153
00:07:39.825 --> 00:07:43.335
Press the raised side of the rocker flat, in one quick press.

154
00:07:43.335 --> 00:07:44.350
One click.

155
00:07:44.350 --> 00:07:48.095
Now the other side is up: that is the side to press next time.

156
00:07:48.095 --> 00:07:52.280
If the rocker stops level, the shutter is open, so press it on down.

157
00:07:52.280 --> 00:07:55.395
A window in the shutter passes the hole as it swings:

158
00:07:55.395 --> 00:07:59.040
a quick press lets light in for about a three-hundredth of a second.

159
00:07:59.590 --> 00:08:01.320
Lesson 5, The shutter.

160
00:08:01.320 --> 00:08:04.025
A shutter lets light in for a set instant;

161
00:08:04.025 --> 00:08:07.212
this one is a plastic blade whose own rim is its spring.

162
00:08:08.933 --> 00:08:10.578
Step four: wind on.

163
00:08:10.578 --> 00:08:15.054
Turn the small green knob the way the picture shows until the arrow on the blue dial

164
00:08:15.054 --> 00:08:16.263
has gone once round.

165
00:08:16.263 --> 00:08:18.728
Keep your other hand off the big red knob.

166
00:08:18.728 --> 00:08:21.413
The arrow points at its mark on the body again.

167
00:08:21.413 --> 00:08:26.433
If the knob is stiff, stop and take your hand off the red knob: never force it.

168
00:08:26.433 --> 00:08:29.479
One turn of the dial is one picture's length of film.

169
00:08:30.029 --> 00:08:32.019
Lesson 6, Winding on.

170
00:08:32.019 --> 00:08:34.654
The film's own holes turn the frame wheel,

171
00:08:34.654 --> 00:08:37.480
so one turn of the dial is exactly one picture.

172
00:08:39.200 --> 00:08:40.020
Two steps.

173
00:08:40.020 --> 00:08:42.363
Then the film goes to a lab to be developed.

174
00:08:42.913 --> 00:08:44.248
The film is finished.

175
00:08:44.248 --> 00:08:49.888
After the last picture, keep turning the small green knob until the arrow on the

176
00:08:49.888 --> 00:08:50.653
dial stops moving.

177
00:08:50.653 --> 00:08:51.903
Then give it three more turns.

178
00:08:51.903 --> 00:08:56.288
The arrow no longer moves: all the film is back in its shell, in the dark.

179
00:08:56.288 --> 00:08:58.908
Only now is it safe to open the back.

180
00:08:58.908 --> 00:09:03.990
If the arrow is still moving, keep winding; never open the back before it stops.

181
00:09:05.700 --> 00:09:06.625
Open the back.

182
00:09:06.625 --> 00:09:09.765
Slide the film out with its knob and pull the knob off.

183
00:09:09.765 --> 00:09:13.450
The film's tip is inside the shell, or just peeping out.

184
00:09:13.450 --> 00:09:17.765
Send the film off with your developing card, or take it to any photo lab:

185
00:09:17.765 --> 00:09:21.380
any lab that develops 35 millimetre film can do it.

186
00:09:21.380 --> 00:09:24.090
Ask for scans, and keep the negatives.

187
00:09:24.090 --> 00:09:25.464
They are the originals.

188
00:09:27.167 --> 00:09:28.532
The pinhole experiment.

189
00:09:28.532 --> 00:09:31.527
Take the pinhole disc from the bag, or make one.

190
00:09:31.527 --> 00:09:36.343
To make one, ask an adult to cut a square about 10 mm across from a clean drinks can

191
00:09:36.343 --> 00:09:39.467
with kitchen scissors, and to snip off its corners.

192
00:09:39.467 --> 00:09:42.037
Lay it on card, press a pin into the middle,

193
00:09:42.037 --> 00:09:44.467
then push just until the tip comes through.

194
00:09:44.467 --> 00:09:48.489
Hold it up to a lamp: you should see one tiny round point of light.

195
00:09:49.039 --> 00:09:50.804
Lesson 1, The pinhole.

196
00:09:50.804 --> 00:09:52.939
Light travels in straight lines,

197
00:09:52.939 --> 00:09:57.779
so a small hole lets through from each point of a scene only the rays lined up with

198
00:09:57.779 --> 00:09:59.301
it: an upside-down picture.

199
00:10:01.033 --> 00:10:02.163
Leave the lens out.

200
00:10:02.163 --> 00:10:05.675
Lay the disc flat in the round pocket, hole in the middle,

201
00:10:05.675 --> 00:10:08.553
and press the pinhole ring in on top of it until it stops.

202
00:10:08.553 --> 00:10:11.998
The disc covers the hole in the floor of the pocket all round.

203
00:10:11.998 --> 00:10:15.058
The ring stands a little proud and does not wobble.

204
00:10:15.058 --> 00:10:19.688
Same plate, same pocket: with the disc and ring it is a pinhole camera.

205
00:10:19.688 --> 00:10:22.575
To change back, lift the ring out with a fingernail.

206
00:10:24.300 --> 00:10:25.580
Set the large dot.

207
00:10:25.580 --> 00:10:27.680
Stand the camera on something steady.

208
00:10:27.680 --> 00:10:33.600
Hold the rocker level to open it, count, then press it down, and wind on.

209
00:10:33.600 --> 00:10:35.405
With ISO 400 film: in sun, open and shut.

210
00:10:35.405 --> 00:10:36.950
Cloud, count 1.

211
00:10:36.950 --> 00:10:38.500
Shade, count 3.

212
00:10:38.500 --> 00:10:40.830
Indoors by a window, count 40.

213
00:10:40.830 --> 00:10:44.850
The pinhole lets in about 150 times less light than the large dot,

214
00:10:44.850 --> 00:10:47.473
so a pinhole picture is counted, not snapped.

215
00:10:49.200 --> 00:10:50.670
That is the whole camera.

216
00:10:50.670 --> 00:10:57.302
The 9 lessons explain how it works, one idea each, at curve35.com/lessons.

217
00:10:57.852 --> 00:11:03.722
The final roll: 24 frames that use every lesson, and a rubric to grade it.

218
00:11:03.722 --> 00:11:06.446
It is at curve35.com/final.

219
00:11:06.996 --> 00:11:11.985
If a step will not go, the help page is at curve35.com/help.

sections.blurb: Ten steps. Steps 1 to 4 make the dark box. Steps 5 to 10 put the orange front plate on it, with the shutter, the wheel and the lens.
Six steps. Do them in the shade, never in bright sun.
Four steps for every picture: choose a dot, aim, press, wind.
Two steps. Then the film goes to a lab to be developed.

The pinhole experiment, for lesson 1: a first picture with no lens. A thin metal disc with a pinhole goes in the lens pocket instead of the lens, held by the pinhole ring. The kit has a disc; or make one from a drinks can and a pin.

steps.name: BUILD 1
steps.do: Lower the spool, red winder up, into the round chamber on the right (seen from behind).
steps.check: The red winder sits on top of the camera and turns.
steps.ifnot: Its plain end goes into the slot in the floor, the winder's neck into the slot in the roof.
steps.why: The spool, its axle and its winder are one piece, because this part takes the most turning force. A collar on its neck rides in a pocket inside the roof: when the back is on, the winder cannot come out.

steps.name: BUILD 2
steps.do: Slide the green winder into the slot on the left.
steps.check: It turns. It only comes out backwards.
steps.why: This winder will turn the film's own spool. Its forked end fits over a bar inside the film.

steps.name: BUILD 3
steps.do: Lay the back down, inside up. Hold the blue frame wheel with its dial just past the edge of the back. Lay its neck in the fork, then slide it toward the long round post until its teeth touch the end of the post.
steps.check: The wheel turns freely. It does not lift out of the fork.
steps.ifnot: If it lifts out, it was not slid home: slide it 3 mm toward the edge, press it down into the fork, slide it back.
steps.why: The film will turn this wheel: its eight teeth sit in the holes along the film's top edge, and one turn of the dial is one picture. Below the wheel, the film slides round the post.

steps.name: BUILD 4
steps.do: Press the back on until both ends click.
steps.check: Two clicks. The back does not pull off. Pinch the two pads and it does.
steps.ifnot: If it will not close, the frame wheel is not seated, or a winder is not fully down.
steps.why: A nub on a springy finger at each end comes up behind a bar on the body. A ridge all round the back sits in a groove: that keeps the light out. This is the dark box. Everything else goes on its front.

steps.name: BUILD 5
steps.do: Lay the front plate face down. Drop the shutter onto the round peg near the top edge, with its rocker (the bar across its top) hanging over the edge.
steps.check: The rocker sits just outside the edge. The shutter swings and clicks.
steps.ifnot: If it will not lie flat, it is upside down: the rocker must stand up toward you.
steps.why: The peg is the shutter's pivot. The shutter's own rim is its spring: a tooth on the rim drops into three notches in the edge of the pocket it lies in.

steps.name: BUILD 6
steps.do: Pick the plate up and hold it flat. Drop the wheel onto the other peg, handle down through the curved slot.
steps.check: The handle sticks out of the front. The wheel clicks into three places.
steps.ifnot: If the wheel will not lie flat, its handle is not in the slot.
steps.why: The wheel carries three holes of different sizes. Its rim is a spring too.

steps.name: BUILD 7
steps.do: Keep the plate flat. Lower the camera onto it, front down, a little high and a little to one side, until its four pockets drop over the plate's four feet.
steps.check: The camera lies flat on the plate. Nothing rocks.
steps.ifnot: If it rocks, move it about a few millimetres. The feet drop in at one place only.
steps.why: Each foot has a hook underneath and a lip on one side. Each pocket is open at one corner only: that is the way in, and the only way out.

steps.name: BUILD 8
steps.do: Pinch camera and plate together and turn them over. Slide the plate sideways until it stops.
steps.check: The point on the plate's top edge is in line with the middle line on top of the camera.
steps.ifnot: If it will not slide, it is not flat on the camera: go back one step.
steps.why: Now the lips on the feet are under the camera's skin. The plate can no longer be lifted off.

steps.name: BUILD 9
steps.do: Slide the plate down until it clicks.
steps.check: One click. Its top edge is level with the top of the camera.
steps.ifnot: If there is no click, press the plate flat against the body while you slide.
steps.why: The hooks are home and a springy tongue has dropped behind a bump. To come off, the plate has to go up past the click, then sideways, then away: a knock cannot do all three.

steps.name: BUILD 10
steps.do: Press the lens into the round pocket on the front, bulge outward, until it stops. (No lens? The pinhole ring goes here instead.)
steps.check: It sits level and stays in when you shake the camera.
steps.ifnot: If it is loose or will not go in, tell whoever made the kit: the pocket is made for one size of lens.
steps.why: Three small ribs in the pocket hold the lens. Nothing else in the camera is held this way.

steps.name: FILM IN 1
steps.do: Pinch the two pads, top and bottom. Lift the back off.
steps.check: The frame wheel comes away with the back.
steps.why: Do this in the shade, never in bright sun.

steps.name: FILM IN 2
steps.do: Slide the green winder out. Push its forked end into the hollow end of the film.
steps.check: Turning the winder turns the spool inside the film.
steps.ifnot: Wrong end? The other end of the film has a peg sticking out.
steps.why: The fork straddles a bar inside the film's spool.

steps.name: FILM IN 3
steps.do: Lower the film and the green winder in together on the left, the film's lip pointing to the middle.
steps.check: The film sits flat in its chamber.

steps.name: FILM IN 4
steps.do: Turn the red winder until the slot in its spool faces you. Pull the film across and tuck its tip into the slot. Give the red winder one turn.
steps.check: The film is caught. It lies over the two curved rails.
steps.ifnot: If the tip slips out, tuck it deeper and turn again.
steps.why: The film lies on a curve around the lens. That curve is why one simple lens can be sharp from corner to corner.

steps.name: FILM IN 5
steps.do: Close the back.
steps.check: Two clicks. Keep it shut until the film is out.
steps.why: The frame wheel's teeth press on the film's top edge. If they are not in the holes yet, the first turn of the winder drops them in.

steps.name: FILM IN 6
steps.do: Turn the red winder the way the picture shows until it stops: about 25 turns for a film of 24 pictures, about 33 for 36. Then leave it alone.
steps.check: While you turn, the arrow on the blue dial goes round and round: the film is moving.
steps.ifnot: If the arrow does not move, open the back in the shade and tuck the film in again. When the winder stops, stop: do not force it.
steps.why: The winder's teeth lean one way: your fingers catch when you turn it the right way and slip the other way. You have wound the whole film out of its shell. Every picture you take will be wound back into the shell, where light cannot reach it.

steps.name: PHOTOS 1
steps.do: Slide the handle on the front to a dot. The chart shows which one, for your film and the light.
steps.check: It clicks at each dot.
steps.why: The dot shows the size of the hole behind it. Each dot lets in about twice the light of the one before. When even the largest is too small for a snap, take a time picture.

steps.name: PHOTOS 2
steps.do: Aim along the middle line on top: from the edge of the pad at the back to the point at the front. The picture fits between the two outer lines.
steps.check: Stand at least two big steps away from what you are photographing.
steps.why: Nearer than that and the picture is not sharp: the focus is fixed.

steps.name: PHOTOS 3
steps.do: Hold still. Press the raised side of the rocker flat, in one quick press.
steps.check: One click. Now the other side is up: that is the side to press next time.
steps.ifnot: If the rocker stops level, the shutter is open: press it on down. (That picture will be too bright.)
steps.why: A window in the shutter passes the hole as it swings. A quick press lets light in for about one three-hundredth of a second. A slow press lets in more.

steps.name: PHOTOS 4
steps.do: Turn the green winder the way the picture shows until the arrow on the blue dial has gone once round. Leave the red winder alone.
steps.check: The arrow points at its mark on the body again.
steps.ifnot: If the winder resists, stop and let go of the red winder. Do not force it.
steps.why: One turn of the dial is one picture's length of film, wound back into the shell.

steps.name: FILM OUT 1
steps.do: After the last picture, keep turning the green winder until the arrow on the dial stops moving. Then three more turns.
steps.check: The arrow no longer moves: all the film is back in its shell.

steps.name: FILM OUT 2
steps.do: Open the back. Slide the film out with its winder and pull the winder off. Send it off with your developing card, or take it to any photo lab.
steps.check: The film's tip is inside the shell, or just peeping out.
steps.why: Any lab that develops 35 mm film can do it.

steps.name: THE HOLE 1
steps.do: Take the pinhole disc from the bag, or make one. Ask an adult to cut a square about 10 mm across from a clean drinks can with kitchen scissors, and to snip off its four corners. Lay it on card, press a pin into the middle to make a dent, then push just until the tip comes through.
steps.check: Hold it up to a lamp: one tiny round point of light, no tear.
steps.ifnot: A tear, or a hole you can see without the lamp: make another. The edges of can metal are sharp: hold it by its flat sides.
steps.why: The best hole for this camera is a quarter of a millimetre across: only the very tip of a pin. Lesson 1 shows why. No heating, no knives: scissors, a pin and a piece of card.

steps.name: THE HOLE 2
steps.do: Leave the lens out (or push it out from behind with the front plate off). Lay the disc flat in the round pocket, hole in the middle, and press the pinhole ring in on top of it until it stops.
steps.check: The disc covers the hole in the floor of the pocket all round. The ring stands a little proud and does not wobble.
steps.ifnot: If the disc will not lie flat in the pocket, snip its corners a little more.
steps.why: Same plate, same pocket: with the lens it is a lens camera; with the disc and ring it is a pinhole camera. To change back, lift the ring out with a fingernail and tip the disc out.

steps.name: THE HOLE 3
steps.do: Set the large dot. Stand the camera on something steady. Hold the rocker level to open it, count, press it down. Then wind on.
steps.check: ISO 400 film. Sun: open and shut. Cloud: count 1. Shade: 3. Indoors by a window: 40.
steps.ifnot: Nothing on the film: count longer next time.
steps.why: The pinhole lets in about 150 times less light than the large dot, so a picture is counted, not snapped. It is sharp at every distance, and a little soft everywhere.
